name: Breathing and pelvic floor
pattern: Slow belly breathing with the diaphragm, and gentle squeeze-and-relax of the pelvic floor, usually lying on your back with knees bent.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat; a pillow under your head.
One hand on your chest, one on your belly.
Let your jaw, shoulders and belly relax.

steps.text: Breathe in slowly through your nose so the belly hand rises and the chest hand stays still.
Breathe out slowly through soft lips; the belly falls.
Pelvic floor: on a breath out, gently squeeze and lift as if stopping wind and urine; hold a few seconds.
Let go fully on the breath in. Relaxing is as important as squeezing.

cues.why: Diaphragmatic breathing uses the diaphragm instead of neck and chest muscles; it is linked to lower stress and better breathing efficiency.

cues.cue: Squeeze and lift, then fully let go.
cues.why: Supervised pelvic floor muscle training cures or improves stress urinary incontinence in women.

cues.cue: Squeeze on the breath out, relax on the breath in.
cues.why: Pelvic floor activity naturally rises with breathing out and falls as you breathe in.

cues.cue: Keep the belly soft; don't bear down or hold your breath.
cues.why: The pelvic floor works together with the deep abdominals; a gentle draw-in, not a hard brace or push, brings it in.

cues.cue: Rest as long as you squeeze.
cues.why: Fatigue makes the squeeze weaker and sloppier.

breathing: In through the nose for about 4 s, out through the mouth for about 6 s.

tempo.note: About 6 breaths a minute. Pelvic floor: hold 3-10 s, rest the same.

mistakes.name: Chest breathing
mistakes.looks: The chest and shoulders rise; the belly stays flat.
mistakes.fix: Hand on the belly; breathe into the hand.
mistakes.why: Neck and chest muscles take over from the diaphragm.

mistakes.name: Pushing down
mistakes.looks: The belly pushes out and you strain as if lifting.
mistakes.fix: Think lift and draw in, not push.
mistakes.why: Bearing down loads the pelvic floor instead of training it.

mistakes.name: Squeezing the glutes
mistakes.looks: The buttocks clench and the hips lift off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Keep the glutes and thighs soft; only the inside lifts.
mistakes.why: Bigger muscles hide a weak pelvic floor contraction.

safety: Pelvic pain, leaking or after childbirth or surgery: see a pelvic health physiotherapist for a check.
Feeling dizzy: breathe more gently and slowly; return to normal breathing.

variants.change: Lying down: easiest to feel and relax.
Upright: harder; good for daily practice.
Quick squeezes: 1 s on, 1 s off, for sudden loads like a cough.

motion.basis: The body does not move: the rig should animate belly rise (in) and fall (out) as a soft-tissue morph, not joint angles. Crook lying pose is standard; 6 breaths a minute is a common slow-breathing rate (estimate).
